User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the LOCALKEY application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

inviteCode.description: The invite code used to register the user.

inviterId.description: Reference to the User who invited this user. (Relationship: User 1:N User (invited))

inviteCount.description: Number of invites the user has available.

Partner.title: Partner
Partner.description: Represents a partner organization that offers deals.

id.description: Unique identifier for the partner entity.

Offer.title: Offer
Offer.description: Represents a specific offer available to users.

id.description: Unique identifier for the offer entity.

partnerId.description: Reference to the Partner offering this deal. (Relationship: Partner 1:N Offer)

imageUrl.description: URL of the image for the offer.

validFrom.description: Date and time the offer becomes valid.

validUntil.description: Date and time the offer expires.

Redemption.title: Redemption
Redemption.description: Represents a user's redemption of an offer at a partner location.

id.description: Unique identifier for the redemption event.

userId.description: Reference to the User who redeemed the offer. (Relationship: User 1:N Redemption)

offerId.description: Reference to the Offer that was redeemed. (Relationship: Offer 1:N Redemption)

partnerId.description: Reference to the Partner where the offer was redeemed. (Relationship: Partner 1:N Redemption)

redemptionTime.description: Timestamp of when the offer was redeemed.

deviceId.description: Device identifier used for anti-fraud measures.

InviteCode.title: InviteCode
InviteCode.description: Represents an invite code that can be used to invite users to the platform.

code.description: Unique identifier for the invite code entity.

inviterId.description: Reference to the User who created the invite code. (Relationship: User 1:N InviteCode)

usedBy.description: Reference to the User who used the invite code.

createdTime.description: Timestamp of when the invite code was generated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and ease of debugging, adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC, and QAPs. The core strategy revolves around denormalization to eliminate `get()` calls in security rules, promoting atomic operations and simplifying access control.

1.  **Users Collection:** Stores user profiles. This uses path-based ownership for user-related data.
2.  **Partners Collection:** Stores partner organization profiles.
3.  **Offers Collection:** Stores offer details, denormalizing partner information (specifically, the `partnerId`) to ensure that offers can be queried and listed efficiently without needing to access partner documents directly.  This supports QAPs as listing offers doesn't require complex filtering based on partner data.
4.  **Redemptions Collection:** Stores redemption records, using path-based ownership under users to easily track user redemptions. The `offerId` and `partnerId` are denormalized to facilitate usage tracking and fraud detection.
5.  **InviteCodes Collection:** Stores invite codes generated by users, using path-based ownership to easily track the codes generated and their usage.
6.  **Roles: Admin:** Dedicated collections `/roles_admin/{uid}` to manage admin permissions. Rules will simply check for the existence of a document to grant admin access.

This design achieves **Authorization Independence** by denormalizing the `partnerId` into the `Offer` documents.  It supports **QAPs** by segregating data (e.g., offers in a single collection) and using denormalized authorization fields, allowing for secure and efficient `list` operations. Path-based ownership is heavily utilized for user-specific data (redemptions, invite codes), making security rules straightforward.
